# Leaderboard

TTS is the standard time-to-solution metric (Ronnow et al. 2014):
$\mathrm{TTS}_p = \bar{t} \cdot \log(1-p) / \log(1-P_s)$, the expected total
time, running independent restarts, needed to be $p$-confident of finding the
best-found energy at least once, where $\bar{t}$ is the mean per-run time and
$P_s$ is the empirical single-run success probability. This site uses
$p = 0.99$, the field's standard convention.

An Energy marked with $^\dagger$ matches a provable ground state (see
[Instance Library](implementation/instances.qmd#verified-ground-states)),
computed independently of any solver run. When the best energy any submitted
run found for that instance does not match the reference energy, the Best
Algorithm column shows "—", since no algorithm can be credited with having
solved it.

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

**Parameters column (Global Annealing / Population Annealing)**

The `parameters` column reported for the Global Annealing (GA) and
Population Annealing (PA) runs above abbreviates the underlying
`summary.csv` fields as follows:

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (GA only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (GA) / `MCS_per_temperature` (PA) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (GA) or at each temperature (PA) |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

**Parameters column (Global Annealing / Population Annealing)**

The `parameters` column reported for the Global Annealing (GA) and
Population Annealing (PA) runs above abbreviates the underlying
`summary.csv` fields as follows:

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (GA only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (GA) / `MCS_per_temperature` (PA) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (GA) or at each temperature (PA) |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

**Parameters column (Global Annealing / Population Annealing)**

The `parameters` column reported for the Global Annealing (GA) and
Population Annealing (PA) runs above abbreviates the underlying
`summary.csv` fields as follows:

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (GA only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (GA) / `MCS_per_temperature` (PA) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (GA) or at each temperature (PA) |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

**Parameters column (Global Annealing / Population Annealing)**

The `parameters` column reported for the Global Annealing (GA) and
Population Annealing (PA) runs above abbreviates the underlying
`summary.csv` fields as follows:

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (GA only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (GA) / `MCS_per_temperature` (PA) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (GA) or at each temperature (PA) |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |

</details>
